sources.entry: YoutubeDL-Server - Web and REST interface to Youtube-DL for downloading videos onto a server. MIT Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: A self-hosted web and REST service that queues yt-dlp or youtube-dl downloads and saves the resulting videos or audio onto a server.
summary.what_it_does: The server is built on starlette and runs a job queue with configurable parallel download workers. It offers a web UI and a REST API to submit single URLs or multi-URL jobs, pick formats and named profiles, and view job logs. Jobs can be stopped, retried, deleted, or filtered by status. The API can also fetch metadata without downloading, list and delete downloaded files, and report server info, formats, and supported extractors. Profiles and reusable option groups (aliases) let you override any yt-dlp/youtube-dl option, such as audio extraction, thumbnails, or subtitles. Upcoming live events and premieres can be parked in a Scheduled status until they start.
use_cases: Download YouTube videos to a home server
Archive online video or audio to a NAS
Save podcasts as MP3 files automatically
Queue video downloads through a REST API
Schedule downloads of upcoming premieres or live streams
how_to_run: cd front && npm install && npm run build
notable: Profiles and option groups (aliases) with a merge order for reusable download presets
Scheduled status for upcoming live events and premieres, with configurable retry interval and max attempts
Choice of yt-dlp or youtube-dl via the YOUTUBE_DL environment variable or Docker tag
Bookmarklets for sending the current page URL to the server
caveats: The README notes the latest youtube-dl release is quite outdated; yt-dlp is the default Docker image
Audio extraction and format conversion require ffmpeg
The server refuses to start if the output path resolves to the filesystem root
